newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Nomura head Sakamaki indicted in sokaiya case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Nomura head Sakamaki indicted in sokaiya case.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors said on Wednesday they had indicted former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki on charges of paying 320 million yen to "sokaiya" racketeer Ryuichi Koike.
They said Nomura itself had also been indicted on charges of violating Japan's Securities and Exchange Law, as had former managing director Nobutaka Fujikura.
Prosecutors said in a statement that Sakamaki and Fujikura had conspired with other Nomura officials to pay 320 million yen in cash to Koike around March 24, 1995.
They said the cash was paid in exchange for assurances from Koike that proceedings at a Nomura shareholders' meeting on June 29, 1995, would go smoothly.
They said the money was handed over in a reception room at Nomura's headquarters in Tokyo.

On June 19, Sakamaki was indicted on charges of making illegal payoffs to Koike of 49.7 million yen between January and June 1995. The company itself as well as Fujikura and another executive had earlier been indicted on a similar charge.
Sakamaki resigned from the top post at Nomura, Japan's biggest brokerage, in March over the scandal, which has also embroiled Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), one of the nation's largest banks.
